legal_name: B. L. Kashyap and Sons Limited
rationale: The firm INR 461.32 cr award is 41.0% of TTM revenue of 1,125.52 cr (stated). It is not routine: it is about 2.4x the largest earlier award in the packet, and FY22 order inflow is about 1x revenue, not a multiple of it. No disqualifier is shown: quarterly PAT was positive for three quarters and the packet shows no default, though the debt position is unknown.

label: HAL
rationale: A firm, company-specific government contract of Rs 3,887 crore for 15 LCH is stated as 16.7% of trailing twelve-month revenue (Rs 23,331 crore), which clears the 10% threshold. It is a binding award, and it is not clearly routine because it is not clearly bigger than the earlier Rs 48,000 crore LCA order, which is the only comparably large award in the packet and is about 12 times larger than this one. The Feb 2021 LCA award and HAL's profitable, AAA-rated position show no stress disqualifier. Confidence is LOW because the packet lacks the order-inflow history and execution timing needed to confirm it is a true change from routine flow.

label: LTTS
rationale: The stated value is USD 100 million or more (multi-year), about INR 750 crore at an assumed INR 75/USD, which is about 11.4% of TTM revenue of INR 6,569.7 crore; the period is not stated, so this is the total, not an annual figure, and the margin is thin above the 10% threshold. The award is firmly awarded to LTTS and opens electric air mobility, a new end market, with a new engineering centre in Quebec, so it is not routine. LTTS is profitable with no stress flag and the customer is external, so no disqualifier applies.

label: SOUTHWEST
rationale: Firm contracts from external state entities total Rs 29.64 crore (ONGC NOA Rs 18.64 cr and SAIL PO Rs 11 cr), about 25.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 117.62 crore; the Rs 7.10 crore Hutti Gold item is only an LOI and is excluded from firmness. The order is clearly bigger than the company's prior Rs 1-5 crore awards and opens geothermal drilling, a first in its history, so it is not routine. The company is profitable (TTM PAT Rs 8.72 crore) with no stress flag, and the event is company-specific with no disqualifier.

label: TATAPOWER
rationale: A firm 1 GW solar EPC contract from SJVN worth about INR 5,500 crore is 12.9% of TTM revenue of INR 42,651 crore, which clears the 10% threshold; the award is to a wholly owned subsidiary, so pass-through applies and the execution risk is recorded. The order is about ten times the largest EPC award disclosed in the packet (INR 538 crore), so it is not routine even though smaller EPC orders recur. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 2,155.61 crore) and the customer is an external government PSU, so no stress or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies.

label: AWHCL
rationale: The NDMC contract is stated at about Rs 1,000 crore over 10 years, which is 154.2% of TTM revenue as a total and about 15.4% a year, clearing the 10% threshold on either basis. It was awarded to a material subsidiary and is firm, though it was first disclosed as an LoI in Dec 2021 and the May 2022 release restates it. It is clearly bigger than any earlier award the company disclosed (Jhansi about Rs 21 crore a year, GNIDA about Rs 23.75 crore), and the company is profitable (TTM PAT Rs 90.40 crore) with no stress flag, so no disqualifier applies.

label: TEXRAIL
rationale: Stated value Rs 6,450 crore over 39 months equals 397.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,621.74 crore; per the rule the multi-year total is compared with annual revenue. The order is firm (bagged from a railway tender) and no comparable order appears in the packet's history, so it is not routine. No disqualifier: TTM PAT is positive at Rs 20.53 crore and the customer is an external state railway; the 39-month phasing and funding remain open for deep research.

label: HGS
rationale: Stated ceiling of Rs 2,100 crore (GBP 211 million) equals 43.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 4,801 crore; the term is unstated, so per the rule the total is compared with annual revenue. The contract is signed and running, company-specific, and no comparable contract appears in the packet, so it is not routine. The ceiling is not committed, the term is unknown and part of the value may already be reported; these are open questions for deep research. The debt-driven finance cost fall is financial and is set aside.

label: STERTOOLS
rationale: Stated order of Rs 600 million equals 11.8% of FY22 revenue of Rs 509.58 crore and is firm (bagged from an external customer). It is not routine: EV MCUs are a new product and customer line, production only began in FY21-22 and the packet shows no comparable order. No disqualifier: the filing calls SGEM a subsidiary and the order book is to be executed in FY23, so it is not fully in reported results. The SGEM ownership split, margin and capex funding are open for deep research.

label: TRITURBINE
rationale: The INR 1.0 billion SADC servicing order is a received contract equal to about 10.8% of trailing revenue of INR 927 crore, so it passes the 10% size test as stated, though the execution period is not given. The company calls it a new aftermarket stream for utility turbines, outside its conventional business, and the packet shows no comparable services order, so it is not routine. It is a maintenance contract with lower margins, and the packet gives no mechanism for margin change, so the margin effect is open.

label: POWERMECH
rationale: The Rs 6,163 crore Adani FGD order is firm and external, and it equals 217% of trailing revenue of Rs 2,834 crore; the total is well above the Rs 343 to 2,120 crore awards disclosed earlier. The company calls it a record order and it adds a new thermal FGD scope, so it is not routine even though the company wins large contracts regularly. No disqualifier applies, and the execution period is the main open question.

label: GENESYS
rationale: The INR 46 crore order is a received, firm government order equal to about 31% of TTM revenue (INR 148.65 crore), with no comparable order in the packet's disclosures, so it reads as a step-change rather than routine flow. No disqualifier applies: the event is external and company-specific, and the company's debt-related cost is small, though trailing losses (PAT -28.91 crore) keep confidence at MEDIUM. Execution period, payment terms and the unexplained earlier margin moves need checking in deep research.

label: JWL
rationale: The INR 514.60 crore order is a firm, received supply order from Indian Railways equal to 43.7% of FY22 revenue (INR 1,178.35 crore), well above the 10% threshold. The packet shows no earlier JWL order of comparable size, so it is provisionally non-routine, although the word 'additional' suggests earlier wagon orders from the same customer that the packet does not show. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the demand is external. Routine status and execution timing need checking in deep research.

label: BAJAJELEC
rationale: The INR 657 crore inflow is firm (orders secured in the quarter), equal to 12.9% of TTM revenue (INR 5,108.79 crore), so it clears the 10% threshold. It is well above the packet's disclosed firm inflows (INR 123 crore in H1 FY22), which makes it a step-change rather than routine flow on available evidence, although it is an aggregate for the quarter. The company is net-debt-free with TTM PAT of INR 190 crore, so no stressed disqualifier applies; deep research should confirm contract-level execution and the PGCIL concentration.

label: SUNDRMFAST
rationale: The USD 250 million EV contract is awarded and is about 42% of FY22 revenue of INR 4,902 crore at an assumed INR 82 per USD, or roughly INR 2,050 crore. It is not routine: the packet shows no comparable prior orders, it opens an EV sub-assembly product line and a new customer segment, and the company calls it its biggest EV contract. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable (FY22 PAT INR 462 crore) and the event is not one-off or internal. Open questions are contract period, firmness of volumes and launch timing.

label: SIEMENS
rationale: The INR 26,000 crore Indian Railways award is firm (a Letter of Award was received) and is 161.1% of FY22 revenue of INR 16,137.80 crore on the multi-year total, so the annual share is lower and the period is not stated. It is not routine: the company calls it its single largest order in India and it opens an electric-locomotive product line that the packet shows no earlier comparable for. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable (FY22 PAT about INR 1,543 crore) and the order is not one-off, internal or already in reported results.

label: IONEXCHANG
rationale: The letter of award from IOCL for Rs 726.13 cr plus GST is firm and external, and it is 39.5% of trailing revenue of Rs 1,838.49 cr, though the total spans about 24 months of build plus O&M and AMC, so the annual impact is smaller. The packet shows no comparable earlier orders, so it is not routine on the packet's evidence, and no stress or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies (the company is profitable, TTM PAT Rs 196.97 cr). Annual split of the contract value is the main open question.

label: FCL
rationale: The Rs 150 cr annual sales value of a secured long-term FMCG order is 30.0% of trailing revenue of Rs 500.70 cr, so it is firm, company-specific and well above the 10% threshold. It is not routine on the packet's evidence, since no comparable order of that size is shown in the company's disclosures apart from a vague 'another order' reference, and it opens a larger home care and hygiene customer relationship. The company is debt-free and profitable, so no stress disqualifier applies; the order itself is not yet visible in reported revenue.

label: WELCORP
rationale: The Anjar TMT plant has started dispatches, so the event is firm (commercial shipment) and company-specific. Size is estimated at about 13.4% of FY2022 revenue from 350 KMT capacity at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed Rs 50,000/t, since the Rs 665 cr figure is backlog and not sizable revenue. It is not routine because TMT bars are a new steel product line, and no disqualifier applies, though the Dec 2022 quarter overlap and funding remain open.

label: SALASAR
rationale: Size: two PVVNL orders total about INR 750 crore against TTM revenue of INR 922 crore, or 81.3% in total over about 24 months (about 40% a year if spread evenly). Firm: received orders from a state utility, a company-specific binding award. Not routine: the largest order previously disclosed in the packet is about INR 252 crore, so this is about 3x any earlier award. No disqualifier; working-capital funding and margins are the open questions.

label: LUMAXIND
rationale: Size: INR 475 crore against TTM revenue of INR 2,261 crore is 21.0%; no execution period is stated, so the total is compared with one year. Firm: binding orders from OEMs against an INR 1,150 crore order book, not a non-binding pipeline. Not routine: the largest comparable order announcement in the packet is INR 250 crore (2021), and the orders are tied to a new facility adding capacity. No disqualifier: TTM PAT is about INR 111 crore; open items are conversion timing, customer identity and funding of the facility.

label: DHRUV
rationale: Size: management's INR 130 crore order total against TTM revenue of INR 80 crore is 161.6% in total; no period is stated, so even over 3 years it is about 54% a year. Firm: LoAs received, and management calls the total its highest ever, so it is not routine on the company's own disclosures. No disqualifier, but the company is very small (market cap about INR 8 crore), the preferential issue is still pending and the total is not itemised in the packet, so confidence is low.

label: BDL
rationale: Size: USD 255M is about INR 2,091 cr at an assumed INR 82/USD, or 68.1% of TTM revenue of INR 3,072.21 cr (periods run to Dec 2022). Firm: a received export order is binding demand. Not routine: no prior export orders appear in the packet, and this is a new market for the company, even though its domestic order sizes are comparable. No disqualifier: the company is profitable with positive PBT in the latest quarters, and the counterparty is external. The main open items are the unnamed counterparty and the FX assumption.

label: VAISHALI
rationale: Size: stated INR 600 cr (USD 73.85M), 871.7% of TTM revenue of INR 68.83 cr, to be executed over 6-8 months. Firm: a received supply order is binding demand. Not routine: the largest prior disclosed orders were about INR 32 cr, and the antibiotics export line is new relative to the packet's history. No disqualifier: the order is not COVID-specific, the company is profitable and not stressed, and the buyer is external. Confidence is LOW because the scale is very large relative to the company, the counterparty is unnamed and funding is unresolved.

label: VOLTAS
rationale: Size: INR 1,770 cr of stated project orders is 19.2% of TTM consolidated revenue of INR 9,208.55 cr; execution period is not disclosed. Firm: the awards are binding orders to UMPESL, a Voltas company, so the revenue lands in consolidated results. Not routine: no earlier project orders of this scale or type appear in the packet, and power distribution and solar EPC is a new revenue stream against the company's appliance and AC business. No disqualifier applies; the company is not stressed, though the Dec-2022 quarter shows exceptional losses, and the customers are unnamed.

label: PARAS
legal_name: Paras Defence and Space Technologies Limited
rationale: Size: INR 64 cr is 35.1% of FY22 revenue of INR 182.56 cr (the packet has no complete trailing four quarters). Firm: the contract was won on 18 Mar 2023 from a domestic government body, with deliveries by FY24. Non-routine on the packet's evidence: no earlier order disclosures appear, so there is no recurring pattern to match it to; whether this is a new product line is not established. No disqualifier applies, though it is unclear whether follow-on orders will follow.

label: TEJASNET
rationale: Size is Rs 696 crore stated against trailing revenue of Rs 746.75 crore, or 93.2%. The order is a received Advance Purchase Order from an external government telecom operator, so it is firm. It is not routine: it is well above the Rs 298 crore PGCIL award, and the company is debt free with about Rs 1,195 crore of cash as of 2021, so it is not stressed. Execution timing and component supply are open questions for deep research.

label: BHEL
rationale: The stated value is Rs 23,000 crore over the contract life, against FY22 revenue of Rs 21,211 crore, or 108.4%; supply alone (80 x Rs 120 crore = Rs 9,600 crore) is still about 45% of that revenue, so the threshold is met either way. The consortium award is a received order from the Ministry of Railways, so it is firm. It is not routine, since it is more than twice the largest earlier award and opens passenger rolling stock. The unresolved items are BHEL's consortium share and execution funding, and the company is profitable in FY22, so it is not stressed.

label: AHLADA
rationale: The stated Rs 124.58 crore (incl. GST) is 87.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 142.23 crore, or about 74% on an ex-GST basis, so the size threshold is met. The contract is a secured government order, so it is firm. It is not routine: prior disclosed orders peaked at Rs 51.36 crore and none since Aug 2021. There is no disqualifier; the company is small and profitable, with PAT of Rs 2.35 crore TTM, though execution funding is unresolved and the share-count data in the packet looks wrong.

label: BSL
rationale: The Rs 250 crore expected additional revenue is stated, equal to 53% of TTM revenue of Rs 471.74 crore; even half that (about 50% utilisation in year one) would be about 26%. The spinning line has commenced commercial operation, so it is firm, and it is not routine because cotton spinning is a new line for the company. The company is profitable (TTM PAT Rs 16.91 crore), so it is not stressed, but the capex of about Rs 200 crore against a market cap near Rs 202 crore leaves funding unresolved.

label: TEXRAIL
rationale: The stated value is Rs 6,450 crore over 39 months against TTM revenue of Rs 2,243 crore, or 287.5% on the total (about 88% a year), so the size threshold is met. The order is received, so it is firm, and it is not routine because it is far larger than any other order in the packet and opens a wagon type the company had not made for a long time. Confidence is low because the same order was first announced on 2022-05-23, and part of its revenue may already be in FY23 results.

label: ENDURANCE
rationale: Rs 9.4 bn of booked OEM orders equals 10.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 8,804 crore (STATED), and booked orders count as firm. It is not routine: the investor presentation shows EV share of orders rising from 12% to 42% with 15 new EV programmes, a new revenue stream compared with earlier disclosures that show only small orders such as EUR 19.3 mn in FY21. The period of the Rs 9.4 bn figure is not stated, and the Rs 6 bn EV figure may overlap it, so the 10.7% uses only the Rs 9.4 bn figure. Balance sheet is not stressed (TTM PAT Rs 480 crore, low finance cost).

label: ALICON
rationale: The FY23 booked orders of Rs 1,700 crore are firm and equal 121.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,401 crore (STATED; execution period not stated, so the figure is a total). It is not routine: the Nov 2021 disclosure gave about 3,000 crore over five years (about 600 crore a year), so FY23 is about 2.8 times that run-rate and adds EV and carbon-neutral customers. Profitable with low finance cost, so not stressed, and no disqualifier applies.

label: ITI
rationale: The Rs 3,889 crore BSNL APO is a received purchase order and equals 220.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,762 crore (total over 24 months; about 110% a year). It is not routine: it is roughly nine times the Rs 433 crore BharatNet order and opens 4G telecom, a new customer and product line. ITI has heavy quarterly losses and finance cost, which could be a stressed-company disqualifier, but an order of this size is plausibly the fix for the cost base, so the disqualifier is not applied; margin and funding are open for research.

label: UNIDT
rationale: Size: INR 720 mn (Rs 72 cr) is 59.8% of TTM revenue of Rs 120.3 cr, a stated value with no execution period. Firm: an award from ONGC in the press release, not a conditional LoI. Not routine: prior disclosed orders were about Rs 10 cr of export and development orders, so a Rs 72 cr single PSU order is a step-change in scale for the product line. No fatal flaw or stress disqualifier (finance cost trivial, still profitable), though liquidity is thin.

label: GREENLAM
rationale: Size: management's full-capacity figure of Rs 400 cr is 19.7% of TTM revenue (Rs 2,026 cr); at 50% year-one utilisation it is about Rs 200 cr, or 9.9%, just under the 10% line. Firm: commercial production started 9 June 2023. Not routine: plywood is a new revenue stream from the Dec 2021 entry announcement and plausibly reaches 10% or more at normal utilisation (19.7% at full capacity). No disqualifier: profitable, and capex financing was tied up in 2022.

label: ASIANENE
rationale: Size: the Rs 78.24 cr LoA is 71.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 110 cr, a stated value. Firm: a letter of award from ONGC with most work in the current financial year. Not routine: the packet shows no seismic work and no similar award since the Feb 2022 Hura and Vedanta contracts, so this is a restart after a 54% revenue fall rather than normal flow. Loss-making, but finance costs are small, so the high-debt stress test is not met; confidence is low given thin data.

label: SANGHVIMOV
rationale: Firm work orders of Rs 150 crore (received, binding) equal 32.9% of TTM revenue of Rs 455.78 crore, which is well above the Rs 35 crore largest order previously disclosed, so this is a step-change rather than routine flow. The counterparties are external IPPs, the company is profitable with PAT of Rs 112 crore TTM, and no disqualifier applies. Execution period is not stated, so the annual revenue contribution is unknown.

label: SHAH
rationale: Received export orders of about INR 40 crore (stated; USD 5 million) equal about 100% of FY2023 revenue of 39.88 crore, with no comparable order in the packet, so it is a step-change rather than routine flow. The company is a weak balance-sheet name (negative net worth until the February 2023 rights issue, related-party loans of about Rs 42 crore, a loss in Q4 FY2023), which is a stress risk, but it is not a disqualifier on the packet alone since the order is operating and the balance sheet is recapitalised. Revenue quality and the delivery period are unknown.

label: ICEMAKE
rationale: A firm award of a Rs 65.48 crore turnkey dairy project (stated, incl. GST) equals 21.0% of TTM revenue of Rs 312.21 crore, or about 18% excluding GST. The only other quantified orders in the packet are Rs 5.20 crore and Rs 1.29 crore, so this is clearly bigger than the company's disclosed flow, though a 2021 AMUL-linked LoI has no stated value to compare. The company is profitable (TTM PAT Rs 20.80 crore) with debt falling and no stress flags, so no disqualifier applies.

label: MIDHANI
rationale: A firm order of Rs 178.54 crore equals 20.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 871.94 crore. The packet shows no earlier quantified orders, and the June 2023 call describes new aerospace customers, so it is not shown as routine business. Revenue was flat and PAT fell about 11.5% in FY2023, and the counterparty and execution period are unknown, so confidence is low. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable.

label: GULPOLY
rationale: Commercial operations at the 500 KLPD plant have started, which is firm, and the packet gives no stated value. Sizing from quantity at 50% year-one utilisation and an assumed Rs 55/litre gives about Rs 502 crore, or 42.5% of FY23 revenue of Rs 1,179.73 crore. This is a step-change in scale over the company's earlier 300 KLPD plan and is not routine. Margin pressure from feedstock and the Q1 FY24 profit fall are open questions for research, not disqualifiers, since the company is not stressed.

label: SONATSOFTW
rationale: A USD 160 million (about INR 1,312 crore at an assumed 82 INR/USD) contract is 17.1% of TTM revenue of 7,685.79 crore, stated in the filing. The company awarded it as a contract win and calls it its largest-ever, far above anything in the packet's earlier disclosures, so it is not routine. The company is profitable with no disqualifier; the unknowns are the contract term and the FX basis, which affect the size estimate.

label: VIKASECO
rationale: The Rs 500m specialty-polymer order is firm (received orders with Aug-Sep 2023 delivery) and equals 13.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 371.67 crore. It is not routine: the disclosed Rs 500m figure is larger than any single order in the packet's history (largest previously Rs 300m, Jan 2022), and it sits in a Jun-Aug 2023 flow of about Rs 990m that is 2.7x TTM revenue. Open questions are the order aggregation, the falling Q1 FY24 revenue, the unexplained margin rise and the coal supply line, which belong in deep research, not in a rejection.

label: BEML
rationale: The Letter of Acceptance from BMRC for Rs 3,177 crore is a firm external award directly to BEML, equal to 83.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,806.68 crore (total value, tenure not stated). It is not routine: the company's recent orders were Rs 378-423 crore, and the 2021 MMRDA order is the only larger one in the packet, with no value stated. Q1 FY24 losses and the unexplained margin rise are open research questions, not disqualifiers, since the company is profitable on a trailing basis.

label: MAHEPC
rationale: Firm award of two contracts worth INR 28.76 crore, which is 13.3% of TTM revenue of 216.30 crore, stated in the filing. No earlier order disclosures appear in the packet, so the order is not routine, and the company's loss-making status is not a disqualifier since debt is low (finance cost about 0.5 crore a quarter). Counterparty and execution terms are unknown, which lowers confidence.

label: EXXARO
rationale: The company says it has bagged an order of Rs 35-40 crore for big-size premium slabs; the low end is 35 crore, or 10.9% of trailing revenue of 321.5 crore, so it clears the 10% threshold. The order is received, so it is firm. The packet shows no earlier order disclosures of this size, and it is tied to the Big Slab line launched Oct 2022, so it is not routine. No disqualifier: the company is profitable on a trailing basis, though PAT is falling. Open questions are the counterparty, timing and margin.

label: JYOTISTRUC
rationale: The company has received an LoA from Apraava Energy for a 400 kV transmission line valued at 260.85 crore including GST. Excluding GST, about 221 crore against trailing revenue of 398.75 crore is 55.4%, so it clears 10%. The LoA is firm. This is not routine: it is about twice the largest earlier order (124 crore) and comes from a new customer. The company's losses are small, its finance cost is low, and no disqualifier applies, though TTM PAT is negative and the company diluted 11%.

label: DYCL
rationale: Size: LoA of 95.91 crore including GST; GST is not revenue to the company, so the ex-GST value of about 81.28 crore is 11.7% of TTM standalone revenue of 691.92 crore (13.9% on the gross figure), above the 10% bar. Firm: a received Letter of Acceptance from Northern Railway, a domestic government customer unrelated to the company, with execution in six months. Not routine: the packet shows no earlier comparable order and the railway signalling cable supply is a new customer category. The Oct 10 disclosure is a GST legal order and is noise; there is no disqualifier and the company is profitable (TTM PAT 35 cr).

label: AAATECH
rationale: Size: order of 4.12 crore against latest full-year revenue of 23.00 crore (FY2023-03), so 17.9% of revenue; no trailing twelve-month figure is available in the packet. Firm: a received order from Punjab National Bank confirmed by the filing. Routine: the packet shows one earlier order of similar size (4 crore, 2020) and no regular order run, so it is not routine on the packet's evidence, though the company's core audit business makes this judgement LOW confidence. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable (FY23 PAT 2.87 crore) and small, so research should test whether bank orders recur.

label: NIPPOBATRY
rationale: Firm awarded contract of Rs 100 crore from BAE Systems, stated as 17.4% of trailing four-quarter revenue of 573.17 crore, so size is material. It opens a new external customer and export defence product line, and the earlier Rs 113 crore order was rail and does not make this routine. The company is loss-making with unknown debt and the JV share is unstated, but neither is a stated disqualifier, so the case goes to deep research on those open points.

label: SOMICONVEY
rationale: The stated order of Rs 46.61 cr is 44.1% of TTM standalone revenue of Rs 105.62 cr (total value, execution period not stated), and it is a firm secured order. The packet has no earlier comparable order disclosures, so it is clearly larger than anything the company has disclosed and is not routine. No disqualifier is evident from the packet, though the buyer is unnamed and related-party demand has not been excluded.

label: VIKASLIFE
rationale: The Gujarat Gas award of Rs 495 mn to subsidiary Genesis is a firm, stated order equal to 10.6% of TTM consolidated revenue of Rs 466.97 cr (execution period not stated). It is clearly larger than any gas-meter order in the packet (the largest earlier was about Rs 55 mn) and marks a shift to ultrasonic meters, so it is not routine. The counterparty is an unrelated external utility, and no disqualifier applies: debt and finance costs are small and the two most recent quarters were profitable.

label: TECHNOE
rationale: Size is the stated INR 1,750 cr award, 141.8% of TTM revenue of INR 1,234.5 cr, though the execution period is not stated. It is firm (awarded, not L1) and company-specific, and it is not routine at this scale: the packet shows no awarded order this large before (prior flows were about INR 600 cr over nine months, and the INR 1,600 cr FGD orders were L1 positions). No disqualifier applies: the company is debt-free and profitable and the client is an external party.

label: HECPROJECT
rationale: A received work order (firm) from RVNL, an external state PSU, worth Rs 62.1 crore against trailing revenue of Rs 59.5 crore, so about 104% of revenue. It is bigger than any order in the packet's history (largest previous Rs 37.0 crore), so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies: the company is small but profitable, and the order is external rather than internal demand. Execution period, margin and funding are unresolved.

label: ASALCBR
rationale: Commercial production of a new 40 MLPA ethanol plant began on 2024-01-13 with OMC orders in hand, so it is FIRM. Size is estimated at about Rs 132 crore (20 ML year-one at Rs 66/litre) against trailing revenue of Rs 699 crore, about 18.9%, above the 10% threshold. It opens an ethanol revenue line to a new customer type and is not routine, and no disqualifier applies, though the order value and realisation are unconfirmed.

label: KIRLOSENG
rationale: A received order from NPCIL, an external government customer, is FIRM. The stated Rs 768 crore total is 14.1% of trailing revenue of Rs 5,452 crore, though it runs over 68 months (about 2.5% a year). It is clearly bigger than the company's previously disclosed orders and opens a new customer, so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable, and the annual contribution is the main open question.

label: ALPHAGEO
rationale: Oil India's INR 57.15 crore award (INR 48.4 crore ex-tax, which is 184% of TTM revenue of INR 26.3 crore) is a firm letter of award and is company-specific. The packet gives no prior order values, so the routine test is uncertain; recent revenue has fallen steeply, which supports treating it as a step-change rather than normal flow. No disqualifier applies, though the company has been loss-making in the last three quarters and the stock is illiquid.

label: DHARMAJ
rationale: Commercial production started 2024-01-22, which is firm. Size is estimated from quantity: 25,500 MT capacity x 50% utilisation x an assumed INR 200/kg gives about INR 255 crore, or 43% of TTM revenue of INR 589 crore, although the internal-use share is not stated and may overstate external revenue. The plant is the company's entry into technicals and intermediates, a new revenue line, so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies; the company is funded and profitable on a TTM basis (PAT INR 44 crore).

label: SASKEN
rationale: USD 29.2M won orders at an assumed 83 INR/USD is about INR 242 crore, or 60.5% of TTM revenue of INR 400.33 crore; using new orders only (USD 18.0M) gives about 37%, still above 10%. The orders are described as won in the quarter, which counts as firm, and the packet shows no earlier order disclosures of similar size, so it is treated as not routine, though this is uncertain. No disqualifier: the company is debt-free and profitable (TTM PAT INR 78.6 crore), although reported revenue is falling.

label: MARINE
rationale: The 104.25 crore order is firm (two received orders) and stated at 19.7% of trailing revenue of 528.16 crore. It is clearly bigger than any single order the company disclosed in the packet (largest prior 43.20 crore; typical orders 2 to 30 crore), so it is not routine flow. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the orders are external, company-specific, and funded by its existing operations.

label: OLECTRA
rationale: Size: 2,400 buses at an assumed INR 1.0 crore each (low end of the Indian e-bus price range) is about INR 2,400 crore, or 193.4% of TTM revenue of INR 1,241 crore; the period is not stated. The LoA is firm, received by EVEY from BMC, an external municipal buyer, and it is treated as Olectra's own firm order as a pass-through because Olectra is the supplier. It is not routine: it is far larger than Olectra's earlier 40-550 bus awards and comes from a major new city customer. Related-party execution, unit price and timing are open, so confidence is medium.

label: HIRECT
rationale: The order is stated as more than Rs 200 crore, about 41.9% of trailing revenue of Rs 477.78 crore (200 / 477.78). The filing is a received domestic supply order from Indian Railways with no related-party interest, so it is firm. It is not routine: the only other disclosed order in the packet is Rs 70.40 crore in 2022. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable on a trailing basis (PAT 4.94 crore).

label: KILITCH
rationale: The USD 9.13 million tender is a firm award to the company's subsidiary by an external government body, so it is firm. At an assumed Rs 83 per USD it is about Rs 75.8 crore, or 48.9% of trailing revenue of Rs 155.03 crore. The packet shows no comparable order disclosure and management describes it as opening government contracts, so it is not routine. The main open question is recurrence, since a single tender could be one-off; no disqualifier applies.

label: WELENT
rationale: A received Letter of Acceptance from BMC, directly to Welspun Enterprises, is firm. Total contract value Rs 4,123.88 crore is 142.4% of trailing revenue of Rs 2,896.25 crore; the packet gives no annual split, so the 48-month plus 15-year period is noted in missing_information. It is not routine: the largest comparable in the packet is a 2021 JV of about Rs 2,500 crore, and this adds a municipal DBO with an O&M annuity. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable on a trailing basis.

label: SOMICONVEY
rationale: The stated order value is Rs 63.296 crore, which is 61.8% of trailing revenue of Rs 102.46 crore (63.296 / 102.46). It is firm: a GeM contract from NLC India, an external central PSU, with a 30,200 metre quantity. It is not clearly routine, since the only earlier comparable is a Rs 46.61 crore bundle, but the one-off nature of a single supply is unresolved, so confidence is LOW.

label: GENESYS
rationale: The stated contract value is Rs 155.85 crore, which is 86.0% of FY2023 revenue of Rs 181.13 crore; trailing four quarters are unavailable because the 2023-09 quarter is missing. It is a firm contract with BMC, but the company's share of the Veritas consortium is not stated, so the size could fall below 10% if its share is small. It is not routine: the largest prior order disclosed in the packet is Rs 76 crore cumulative (Saudi Arabia, 2023). No disqualifier is evident, but the consortium split and contract period are open questions.

label: DJML
rationale: Stated order value is Rs 6.00 crore over 5 years (page 2 of the 19 Apr 2024 filing); the 5-year total is 11.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 53.01 crore, while the annual share is about 2.3%. The order is received (binding demand) from an external insurer and is more than twice the largest earlier disclosed order (Rs 2.5 crore), so it is not routine. No disqualifier found: TTM PAT is positive and the company is not stressed on the packet's figures.

label: DCXINDIA
rationale: The stated order of about US$55.13 million is INR 457.6 crore at the packet's 83/USD rate, or about 32.1% of TTM revenue of 1,423.58 crore. It is a received purchase order, so firm, and it comes from a new overseas customer, much larger than the company's other disclosed orders (for example the US$2 million Lockheed PO), so it is not routine. No disqualifier applies, and the company is profitable with the debt reduced and QIP proceeds raised, but the period of execution and production readiness are open questions for deep research. The earlier 28.3% figure was miscalculated and is replaced here.

label: RPTECH
rationale: The INR 1,510 crore NMDC Data Center order was accepted as purchase/work orders on 3 April 2024, so it is firm, and it equals 13.6% of FY24 revenue of INR 11,094.70 crore. The company calls it its largest ever single order and it opens a data-centre project segment, so it is not routine. Company is profitable (FY24 PAT INR 143.86 crore) and no disqualifier applies; open items are margin, execution period and working capital.

label: GVT&D
rationale: Size: the largest listed Q4 FY24 order is INR 57,912 million (about 5,791 crore), roughly 183% of trailing revenue of 3,167.91 crore, though the period over which it executes is not stated. Firm: the orders are received orders from named customers. Not routine: the packet's earlier disclosed orders run about 370 to 800 crore, and management calls this the highest inflow in a decade, so these are clearly bigger than anything disclosed before. No disqualifier: the company is debt-free with profits in FY24, the customers are external utilities and EPCs, and the demand is not one-off.

label: DREDGECORP
rationale: Firm award from SMPA of 2,015.88 INR crore for five years of maintenance dredging. The total is 213.2% of trailing revenue of 945.50 INR crore (about 42.6% a year). The packet shows no comparable award before, so it is not routine. The counterparty is an external government port authority and there is no stress or other disqualifier; the signed contract and annual phasing are open.

label: MANORAMA
rationale: Commercial production has started at a new 25,000 TPA fractionation plant, which makes it firm (capacity commissioned and operating). Sized at 25,000 TPA x 50% utilisation x an assumed Rs 250/kg realisation, it is about Rs 312.5 crore, or about 68% of TTM revenue of Rs 457.08 crore, so the estimate is sensitive to the price assumption. This is a step-change in the company's fractionation line (about +167% capacity), not routine flow, and no disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and the packet shows no stress.

label: RAMKY
rationale: The INR 1,297 crore HMWSSB contract, awarded to a subsidiary of the company, equals 60% of TTM revenue of INR 2,161 crore (contract period not stated, so this is a total-value comparison). It is an external government award, so it is firm and counts as the company's own order under the pass-through rule. The largest prior award in the packet is about INR 107 crore, so it is non-routine and opens a build-and-operate wastewater stream. Funding and the balance sheet are not in the packet, but the company is profitable and no heavy-loss disqualifier applies, so deep research is warranted.

label: SONACOMS
rationale: The INR 680 crore order is a received order equal to about 20% of TTM revenue of 3,346 crore, and it is larger than the company's previous largest single order (INR 501 crore EDL program), so it is not routine. It also adds a first order in a new sensors and software product line for electric CVs. The company is profitable with TTM PAT of 547 crore and low finance cost, so no stress disqualifier applies, though the execution period is not stated. Sized on total value against TTM revenue; the period is unknown.

label: FILATFASH
rationale: The USD 35 million purchase order (about INR 292 crore at an assumed INR 83.5/USD, over a 7-year term) is firm, received by the subsidiary from an external buyer, and equals about 166% of FY24 revenue of INR 176.41 crore on the stated total (about 24% a year). It is the subsidiary's first export order and opens a new marble revenue line, so it is not routine. Counterparty payment capacity and mining output are open questions for research, not disqualifiers.

label: ANUP
rationale: The two orders together exceed INR 100 crore, are received (firm), and equal 17.6% of annual revenue as stated in the packet (24.3% on FY23 revenue of INR 411.34 crore), above the 10% threshold. The packet has no earlier order-win disclosures, so there is no evidence of routine order flow, and the orders are not shown to belong to a related party. Confidence is low because the customer is unnamed and execution terms are unknown.

label: EMSLIMITED
rationale: Size: the 535.19 crore LoA, taken at EMS's 95% share (508.4 crore), is 59.0% of trailing four-quarter revenue of 861.62 crore; the value covers construction plus an 18-year O&M period, so the annual share is lower than this total and the ratio compares totals as the rule requires. Firmness: a letter of award for a JV that EMS leads at 95%, so firm. Not business as usual: the company's disclosed tenders are mostly L-1 or small-ticket, and this is clearly larger than anything shown, adding a water supply and sewerage O&M revenue stream, so it is not routine. No disqualifier is present; the company is profitable (TTM PAT 167.34 crore), not stressed.

label: MANAKCOAT
rationale: A signed European contract worth about 200 INR crore is 26.3% of trailing revenue of 761.73 INR crore, with the execution period not stated. The packet shows no comparable order in the company's history, and the company itself calls it landmark and export-led, so it is not routine. The company is not stressed: debt is low, the rating was upgraded, and the preferential issue is funding growth; the open items are recurrence and execution timing.

label: ZODIAC
rationale: The INR 154.27 crore Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation order is firm (received 7 October 2024) and is an external government award, equal to 57.7% of TTM revenue of INR 267.30 crore over its five-year term (about 11.5% a year). It is clearly bigger than any order the packet shows the company disclosing and opens a utility-scale solar build and O&M revenue stream, so it is not routine. The company is profitable and has a QIP completed, so no stress disqualifier applies; EPC/O&M split, timing and margin are open.

label: TDPOWERSYS
rationale: The INR 300 crore five-year traction-motor contract, read from the Q2 FY25 call transcript, is 27.6% of TTM revenue of INR 1,087 crore on a total-value basis (about 5.5% per year), and management says contracts are signed. Traction motors are a new product line and facility, so it is not business as usual, unlike the routine export motor and geothermal orders. The company is debt-free and profitable, so there is no stress disqualifier; prototype clearance and the facility decision are the open items.

label: DHRUV
rationale: The MSIDC letter of award is firm and its stated fee of Rs 23.46 crore over 90 months is 28.8% of FY24 revenue of Rs 81.50 crore (total against annual revenue, as the rules require; about 3.8% a year). It is not routine: the ticket is about 1.7x the largest contract disclosed before, and the company's typical awards were Rs 3-11 crore. The fee is for a consortium project, and the company's JV share is unstated, so the size is an upper bound that stays above 10% only if its share is at least about 35%. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable and has just completed an equity raise.

label: PENIND
rationale: Size: the Raebareli plant adds about 25% (low end of 25-30%) to production capacity; at a conservative 50% first-year utilisation on the current revenue base of 3,048.61 crore, that is about 12.5% (about 381 crore), estimated from capacity as the rule allows. Firmness: the plant is commissioned, which is firm. Not business as usual: management describes earlier plant additions as a few crores each, and this one is the stated driver of the revenue recovery after a delay, so it is a step-change in capacity. The 986 crore and 416 crore order readings are rejected as aggregate or segment figures, and no disqualifier applies.

label: RATNAVEER
rationale: The INR 180 crore of orders is about 23% of TTM standalone revenue of 769 crore and is stated as received, so it is firm and above the 10% threshold. No comparable order disclosure appears in the packet, and the Phase 1 expansion adds capacity for them, so it is not routine. The company is profitable with TTM PAT of 40 crore and cheap finance cost, so no stress disqualifier applies, but the customer, order count and margin are unknown and the orders have not been identified as a single contract.

label: EXICOM
rationale: Stated value INR 1,680 crore is a multi-year total (about 3 years of equipment plus 10 years of services) and is about 186% of TTM revenue of INR 902.98 crore (1,680 / 902.98). It is an advance purchase order received from system integrators, so firm, and it is the largest order the company has disclosed, a step-change from a critical power business described as sluggish, so not routine. Losses (TTM PAT -20.30 crore) and dilution are noted, but the packet shows no default or going-concern signal; funding is unresolved and the period is contradictory across filings.

label: PPAP
rationale: The INR 192.8 crore of received lifetime orders is firm and equals about 35.5% of TTM revenue of INR 542.49 crore, although the execution period is not stated, so the annual run-rate is uncertain. It is not routine on the packet's history: the only prior sized announcement is INR 118 crore, and the EV orders and new KIA footprint open a new revenue stream. The company is loss-making on TTM PAT (INR -3.58 crore) but carries no heavy debt or distress evidence, so no disqualifier applies; funding for execution is unresolved.

label: RITCO
rationale: Size: the stated INR 120 crore contract is 11.7% of TTM revenue of INR 1,022 crore (execution period not stated, so this is total value against one year of revenue). It is firm because the release says the contract is secured. It is not routine on the packet's evidence, since no earlier order of this size is disclosed, and it opens a new contract stream. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 36 crore) with funds raised in 2024, so no stress disqualifier applies; the main open questions are execution timing and margin.

label: CENTUM
rationale: Size: the stated INR 300 crore contract is 27.7% of TTM revenue of INR 1,083.92 crore (the packet's own figure is 27.2%; the difference is rounding or base). It is firm because management says the company has won it. It is not routine: the largest disclosed prior orders are DRDO payload orders without values or a ~INR 80 crore delivery in 2024, so this is clearly bigger and opens a satellite-payload EW line. Losses (TTM PAT -30 crore) and a pending fund raise are risks, but the debt level and the FY24 customer advances do not make it a stressed company, so no disqualifier applies.

label: ACE
rationale: A firm INR 420 crore MoD contract equals about 13.1% of TTM revenue of INR 3,202 crore, with the execution period not stated. It is not routine: the company calls it its largest order ever and the earlier MoD orders in the packet were a fraction of this size (99 forklifts; 285 forklifts and 6 cranes). The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 389 crore), debt-free and funded, so no stress disqualifier applies; the main open questions are the delivery schedule and whether such procurement recurs.

label: AWHCL
rationale: Size is INR 976 crore against TTM revenue of INR 901.13 crore, about 108% (packet says 111.5%; the contract period is not stated, so this is total value against one year of revenue). The award is firm: an external Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation contract to wholly owned subsidiary AG Infra, a pass-through, with revenue phasing in. It is not routine, since the largest C&T award in the packet history is INR 386 crore (Panvel, Oct 2023); the open question is whether it adds revenue or re-tenders an existing contract. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 84.80 crore), so no stressed-company disqualifier applies, though funding is unresolved given its debt.

label: ADROITINFO
rationale: Stated value INR 6.20 crore against TTM revenue of INR 29.02 crore is about 21.4% (execution period not stated, so this is not annualised). The order is a received SAP services contract, so firm. It is not routine: it is clearly larger than any order disclosed in the packet (previous maximum INR 3.78 crore, most INR 1 to 2.5 crore), although the company does win similar SAP services orders regularly, so this is a borderline call. Stressed balance-sheet and fatal-flaw tests do not apply on the packet; the company is profitable on a TTM basis and rights-issue funds are raised.

label: SWELECTES
rationale: Orders for over 150 MW of modules are received (firm) and, at an assumed INR 14 per Wp, are worth about INR 210 crore, or roughly 44% of TTM revenue of INR 478 crore; the packet gives no stated value, so size is estimated. The order is well beyond the company's prior commissioned plants (4 to 12 MW each), so it is not routine. Losses in the latest quarter, heavy finance cost and the share price fall are risks, but the company is TTM profitable and funded by the INR 290 crore raise, so no disqualifier is applied; the counterparty must be confirmed as external.

label: REFEX
rationale: Stated value INR 750 crore against FY25 revenue of INR 2,467.66 crore (TTM equal to FY25) is about 30.4%, to be executed in FY26. It is a received order from an external utility (Torrent Power), so firm, though the packet's record conflicts on this and the value is management-stated. It is not routine: the release calls it the first major order for wind turbine supply, a new product line for the group. Pre-existing earnings are strong (FY25 PAT INR 158 crore), and equity raised in the preferential issue, so no stress or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies.

label: JBMA
rationale: The company has won an order for 1,021 electric buses with an approximate value of INR 5,500 crore, about 100% of TTM revenue of INR 5,472 crore; the value period and any O&M split are not stated. The order is firm and is far larger than the company's earlier 43-bus order, so it is not routine. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 215 crore), though finance cost is heavy, and no stress or one-off disqualifier applies; the flagged dilution is a stock split.

label: REMSONSIND
rationale: Size is INR 300 crore (USD 35 million) against TTM revenue of INR 351.40 crore, about 85% (packet says 90.6%; the execution period is not stated, so the annual impact could be lower). The order is firm (secured from Stellantis North America). It is not routine: the prior disclosed orders were about INR 30 crore each (Tata Motors, sensor LoI), so this is roughly ten times larger and opens a new large North American OEM customer. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 14.97 crore) with low finance cost, so no stressed disqualifier applies.

label: WEBELSOLAR
rationale: Stated INR 623 million (INR 62.3 crore) against TTM revenue of INR 575.45 crore is about 10.8%, just above the 10% threshold; the packet's 22.2% figure does not reconcile. The order is firm (secured orders with stated value), and it is not clearly routine, since the company had no quantified orders before and its shipments reach export markets not shown earlier. Confidence is low: order counterparty, timing and whether it is one contract or several are unknown, and recent orders are arriving in quick succession.

label: SALZERELEC
rationale: The Rs 192 cr BBMP work order is firm (a received work order) and company-specific, and it is 13.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,418.33 cr when the total is compared as the rule requires, though it runs to 2032, so the annual share is only about 2% a year (the packet's own framing). It is not routine: it is several times the size of any order disclosed before, with a new municipal customer type. No disqualifier applies, but execution cash flow and margin are unknown, and the annual effect is much smaller than the total, which is the main research question.

label: AARON
rationale: The company's own estimate of Rs 150 Cr additional revenue from the capacity expansion is about 192% of TTM revenue of Rs 77.93 Cr, although the period is unstated and the packet flags it as non-binding. The expansion is firm in the sense that capacity has been commissioned and Unit 3 has started commercial operations, and a doubling of the plant base is clearly bigger than the company's disclosed history (revenue Rs 55.85 Cr in FY23, Rs 63.23 Cr in FY24). The Rs 419 Cr order tag is a misread of market cap, and no disqualifier applies (PAT Rs 8.24 Cr, debt-equity 0.19).

label: GULFPETRO
rationale: Size is INR 225 crore against TTM revenue of INR 609.27 crore, about 37% (the contract period is not stated, so this is total value against one year of revenue). The contract is firm: a secured bitumen supply contract with HPCL. It is not routine on the packet, which shows no earlier order announcements of this size, but confidence is LOW because the period may be short and the contract could replace existing spot sales. No stressed or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies: the company is profitable with low finance cost.

label: BAJEL
rationale: The 2,600 crore 765 kV order is stated as received and equals 100.1% of FY25 revenue of 2,598.24 crore; no execution period is given, so the total is compared as the rule requires. It is not routine: the largest disclosed order before was about 586 crore, and 765 kV work is a new voltage class for the company. No disqualifier is visible; deep research should confirm the LoA status, the execution period and working-capital needs.

label: POLYCAB
rationale: The executed BSNL agreement is a firm government award, with consideration of INR 6,447.54 crore including GST, or about INR 5,464 crore ex-GST, which is about 24% of TTM revenue of INR 22,408 crore. It is not routine: it is many times the company's prior government order flow (RDSS revenue of INR 964 crore in FY24) and opens a build-and-operate network revenue stream. The company is highly profitable (TTM PAT INR 2,046 crore) with no stress, so no disqualifier applies; the execution period and capex/opex split are the open questions.

label: AXISCADES
rationale: The Rs 600 Cr cumulative order value is a received order from defence laboratories, equal to 58.3% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,029.96 Cr in total, or about Rs 120-200 Cr a year over three to five years (roughly 12-19% of revenue a year). It is not routine: the largest order the company has disclosed before was Rs 90 Cr (BEL, May 2024), and this award spans new airborne, naval and radar programmes. No disqualifier applies; the company is profitable (FY25 PAT Rs 75.28 Cr) and debt was largely repaid from the QIP.

label: MENONBE
rationale: The Rs 30 cr US order is stated and firm (secured, with production due to start), and it is 12.1% of TTM revenue of Rs 248.80 cr, so it clears the 10% threshold. It is not routine: the company's prior disclosed orders were unvalued samples and tooling, and a Rs 30 cr order from a new US customer is a step-change for a company with revenue around Rs 240 cr a year. No disqualifier applies; the company is lightly indebted, but the execution period and margin on this order are open.

label: DIVGIITTS
rationale: The 800 crore lifecycle contract is firm; comparing the seven-year total with TTM revenue of 236.36 crore, as the rule requires, gives 338.5% (about 48% a year). It is not routine: it is larger than any single order disclosed before (the largest single one was about 47 crore) and sits in the core transfer-case line. No disqualifier is visible, but the order was first disclosed in Aug 2024, so deep research should check prior triage status.

label: COSMOFIRST
rationale: The BOPP line is commissioned and running, so it is firm, and its estimated revenue is about Rs 487 cr a year (16.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,005.46 cr), using 81,200 MT capacity, 50% year-one utilisation and a low-end Rs 120/kg realisation that the packet does not give. It is not routine: at 81,200 MT it is about 2.7x the earlier BOPET line and 3.7x the CPP line, and it lifts the company's core BOPP volume by about 40%. No disqualifier applies, although debt is high and the realisation assumption and ramp timing are open.

label: PTCIL
rationale: A firm order of over INR 100 crore from BrahMos Aerospace is about 28% of TTM revenue of INR 358 crore, with the execution period not stated. It is not routine: none of the company's earlier defence orders in the packet was disclosed with a value, and BrahMos is a new customer for a new casting product. The company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 61 crore) and funded, so no disqualifier applies; the main open questions are the delivery schedule and margin.

label: PREMEXPLN
rationale: Size: the firm order inflow of about INR 330 crore is 69.2% of TTM revenue of INR 477 crore (79% of FY25 revenue of INR 417 crore), so it clears 10% by a wide margin. Firmness: these are received orders from BrahMos and overseas clients, so they are firm. Not routine: the company's previously disclosed orders were tens of crores, and this is a step up in scale in rocket motors and propellant. No disqualifier is evident; the execution period, split between customers and the QIP funding remain open questions for deep research.

label: SIGNPOST
rationale: The nine-year exclusive contract with BMRCL is a received award, and its stated revenue potential of up to Rs 700 Cr is 142.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 490.40 Cr in total, or about 15.9% a year at the ceiling. The packet shows no comparable metro contract in the company's history, so the network is a new revenue stream rather than routine flow. The figure is a ceiling on gross potential rather than committed revenue, so deep research must test the minimum guarantee and the net share; there is no disqualifier and the company is profitable (FY25 PAT Rs 33.90 Cr).

label: NETWEB
rationale: The 1,734 crore order is stated as secured and is 133.3% of TTM revenue of 1,300.92 crore, with execution due between Q4 FY26 and H1 FY27, so it is a near-term step-change. It is not routine: the largest disclosed order before was about 147 crore, and the order opens a sovereign-AI infrastructure segment. No disqualifier is shown; deep research should check the counterparty, hardware margin and working capital.

label: SJVN
rationale: Size: the 660 MW unit at a conservative 50% year-one load factor and an assumed INR 3.5/kWh gives about INR 1,012 crore a year, or 32.4% of TTM revenue of INR 3,125 crore. Firmness: the unit is synchronised, has run a 72-hour full-load test and was inaugurated, and management said COD was days away, so it is treated as commissioned, though no formal COD notice is in the packet. Not routine: a thermal plant is a new revenue line for SJVN, and no disqualifier applies (PAT is positive, though finance cost is rising sharply).

label: RAMKY
rationale: Size is INR 2,085 crore against TTM revenue of INR 1,854.65 crore, about 112% (packet says 98.4%); the execution period is not stated, so this is total value against one year of revenue and annual impact may be lower under a multi-year HAM. The order is firm (secured from HMWSSB under HAM). It is not routine: the largest comparable award in the packet is INR 1,297 crore from the same client in 2024, and this is larger. No disqualifier applies, since TTM PAT is INR 216.55 crore, though revenue is weakening and funding is unresolved.

label: THEJO
rationale: The 129 crore three-year O&M order is stated as booked; as the rule requires, the three-year total is compared with TTM revenue of 577.43 crore, giving 22.3% (about 7.4% a year). It is not routine: earlier orders were 2 to 4 crore, and this is a long-term service contract at a major steel plant, a new revenue stream. No disqualifier is visible; deep research should test the annual run-rate and margin, since the total overstates the per-year effect.

label: PARAS
legal_name: Paras Defence and Space Technologies Limited
rationale: Size is INR 39.63 crore (35.68 plus 3.95) against TTM revenue of INR 392.91 crore, about 10.1%, a marginal pass; the parent order alone is 9.1%. Both orders are firm and due by May 2026. They are not routine because counter-drone is a new product line for the company (MicroCon MoU Apr 2025, CERBAIR counter-UAS LoI Jul 2025), so the first MoD orders are a product step-change, though earlier defence orders of INR 30 to 65 crore were routine. No stressed or fatal-flaw disqualifier applies, but confidence is LOW because the size sits on the 10% line.

label: JASH
rationale: The approximately INR 77 crore order for 96 knife gate valves is about 10.05% of TTM revenue of INR 766 crore, which just meets the threshold, and the filing describes it as received. It is not routine: the largest single order previously disclosed was about INR 48 crore, and monthly order intake has been INR 40-80 crore in total. The packet tags it non-binding and the execution period is unstated, so the firmness and size are both borderline; the company is profitable and funded, so no disqualifier applies.

label: MUKKA
rationale: The Rs 474.89 cr BSWML contract is firm: it was awarded by a government body to the company's JV, and the execution period is not stated. Measured against TTM revenue of Rs 1,100.08 cr it is 43.2%, which is an upper bound because Mukka's stake in the JV is not disclosed; it still clears the 10% threshold unless its share is below about 23%. It is not routine: it opens a new waste-treatment line and is about ten times the largest prior order in the packet. Funding and JV economics are open, and the packet's own 'share count up 29,900%' flag is unexplained, so research should start with the JV stake and contract terms.

label: UNIMECH
rationale: The stated order value of INR 72.20 cr against TTM revenue of 247.24 cr gives 29.2%, well above 10%. The subsidiary has received the award, so it is firm; the award goes to a wholly owned, consolidated subsidiary from an external PSU customer, so pass-through is not needed. It is not routine: management describes historical order wins of USD 0.5-1 million and the largest disclosed order was about INR 35 cr, so this award is about twice the largest before. No disqualifier: the company is profitable (TTM operating margin 33%), the award is not in the Sep-2025 results, and no internal or fatal flaw is shown; execution period, margin and the order-book figures are open for deep research.

Firm work order of approx 30.38 crore from unrelated Powerstatic Solutions (Sanand factory, 8-month execution, no promoter interest) is 53.7% of FY25 revenue of 56.53 crore; a second firm 21.67 crore Stynerix order (24 months) takes the Nov-Dec 2025 inflow to about 92% of FY25 revenue. It is not routine on the packet's evidence because no earlier order was quantified and the prior site-work orders look small, and the company has positive PAT and about 10% operating margin with no stress, so there is no disqualifier. Open questions are margin on the new work, working capital, and why the stock fell 72% in a year.

label: CEIGALL
rationale: The Letter of Award is firm and the 1,089 crore project cost is 31.5 percent of TTM revenue of 3,452.52 crore, multi-year total. The company is profitable and has no disqualifier, though TTM revenue growth is not shown and the order book check found no company total in the listed documents.

label: RITCO
rationale: The stated total of about 205 crore is 16.7% of TTM revenue of 1,231.06 crore, and the update describes the contracts as secured, so it is firm. The company wins contracts of similar size regularly, so the order is routine, but the thin TTM margin (7.5%) and cheap valuation (about 0.59x TTM revenue) bring it under the exception, which is decided as not routine since TTM revenue growth is 31.9%. No disqualifier is found; the order book check found no company-total figure, so those fields are null.

label: AWHCL
rationale: Size: the two BMC contracts total about Rs 1,330 crore over seven years, which is 137% of TTM revenue of Rs 968.97 crore on the total (about 20% per year). Firmness: both are awarded contracts from BMC, so they are firm; the subsidiary was merged into the company on 31 Dec 2025. Routine: the company wins multi-hundred-crore municipal C&T contracts regularly, so it is routine under step 3, but its market cap is 1.40x TTM revenue (below 1.5x) and TTM revenue growth is 10.2%, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and the order is decided as not routine. No disqualifier: the company is profitable with a 20.6% TTM operating margin and no losses, though its leverage and the vehicle capex to deliver the contracts are open questions.

label: POWERMECH
rationale: The firm base revenue of INR 1,563 cr (per the press release, read with the page command) is 27.3% of TTM revenue of 5,722.53 cr; the packet's 54.6% uses 3,126 cr, which includes an uncommitted greenshoe. The total is compared over the 15-year contract, as the multi-year rule requires. The award to the lead member is firm, although the BESPA signing is still to come. It is not routine: the company calls this its debut in energy storage and a new vertical, and no BESS award appears in the packet. No disqualifier applies: the company is profitable, and the open questions are the BOO capex funding, the BESPA timing and consortium shares.

label: PANACEABIO
rationale: Size: US$35.65m stated, about Rs 303 crore at the packet-implied 85/USD, which is 50.1% of TTM revenue of Rs 603.85 crore (about 25% per year over the two stated years). Firm: it is a UNICEF Letter of Award, so it is firm. Not routine: it is clearly bigger than the prior stated UNICEF award of US$14.95m, and it is a multi-year LTA; the thin TTM operating margin (1.1%) and TTM revenue growth above zero would also send it to deep research under the exception. No disqualifier: the counterparty is a customer and the demand is a recurring UNICEF programme, not one-off, and the company is loss-making but the finance cost is small.

label: CMSINFO
rationale: The stated total of INR 1,000 cr over a 10-year contract is 41.0% of TTM revenue of 2,436.58 cr; the multi-year rule compares the total and notes the period, and the annual average is about 4.1%. The SBI contract is awarded, so it is firm. It is not routine: the largest single disclosed contract before this is about INR 800 cr, so 1,000 cr is larger, although the company's aggregate wins run at about INR 500 cr a quarter. No disqualifier applies: the company is debt-free with over INR 1,000 cr of cash and is not stressed, and the open questions are the small annual uplift, flat revenue and PSU-bank execution delays.

Size: Rs 92 crore stated, which is 39.0% of FY25 standalone revenue of Rs 235.75 crore (contract period not stated). Firmness: it is an awarded government work order, so it is firm. Not routine: the company announced seven orders worth about Rs 40 crore combined in June 2025, but the largest single order it has stated before is Rs 21.8 crore, so Rs 92 crore is a clear step-change, and it is its first state-government order of this size. No disqualifier: the counterparty is a state government and the company is profitable (FY25 PAT Rs 14.17 crore), though the Tirth Yatra programme's recurrence and the revenue decline are open questions.
