The subsidiary has received the POs, so they are firm; the customers are external (Sipradi Yatri and Magna Automotive, a Tata Motors supplier) and the filing states no related-party or promoter interest. It is not routine because no earlier comparable order is disclosed and the order is about two quarters of the company's revenue. No disqualifier is shown, but the sizing base excludes the subsidiary's revenue, the PO values are internally inconsistent, and the company is tiny and illiquid, so confidence is LOW.

The firm LoA from HESCOM (an external state utility) is stated as INR 70-75 crore over 25 years, which is 54.0% of TTM revenue of 134.30 crore on the total-versus-annual basis the rule requires; the annual run-rate is only about INR 2.9 crore (about 2%), a weakness to test. It is not routine because it opens a new recurring power-generation revenue stream, and the thin TTM operating margin (6.9%) would also allow it under the margin exception. No disqualifier is found, but project capex, funding and the commercial operation date are unknown, so confidence is LOW.

label: MANINDS
rationale: Size: Rs 550 crore stated, 15.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 3,526.65 crore. Firm: the company says it has received the orders (binding demand). Routine by pattern: the company booked Rs 1,850 crore (Jul 2024), Rs 1,150 crore (Jun 2025) and Rs 1,700 crore (Sep 2025) orders, but the market cap of about 0.73x TTM revenue is below 1.5x, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and the order is decided as non-routine, with TTM revenue growth +10.3% above zero. No disqualifier: the counterparty and execution period are open questions for deep research, and the company is funded by the Rs 255 crore preferential issue.

label: SHAKTIPUMP
rationale: Size: the 600.58 crore Letter of Award (ex-GST) is 23.1% of TTM revenue of 2,602.94 crore, with no stated execution period. Firm: a received Letter of Award from a state renewable agency under PM-KUSUM. Not routine: it is about 5.6 times the largest domestic PM-KUSUM award in the packet (107.33 crore ex-GST, April 2025) and about twice the USD 35.3 million Uganda contract (January 2025), and it opens a new state customer. No disqualifier: PM-KUSUM is a recurring government programme, and the company is profitable with a 292.6 crore QIP closed in July 2025 (funding shown as FUNDED).

label: TROM
rationale: Size: Rs 25.79 crore stated, 27.6% of FY25 revenue of Rs 93.32 crore (no TTM revenue in the packet; value includes GST). Firm: the company has received a purchase order from Vimal Electronics (binding demand), first disclosed on 2026-01-08. Not routine: it is about 1.7 times the largest earlier order in the packet, Rs 14.90 crore, and is a grid-connected solar EPC award in Rajasthan. No disqualifier is evident, but TTM margins, funding and the buyer's related-party status are not shown, and the stock is very illiquid.

label: DEEM
rationale: Size: Rs 23.05 crore stated, 24.8% of FY25 revenue of Rs 92.91 crore (no TTM revenue in packet). Firm: the company has received the orders from SAIL and RINL, which are external state-owned customers, so it is binding demand. Not routine: the packet shows no comparable orders before, and the commissioning of Unit II on 2 January 2026 is a new operating base. No disqualifier is evident, but the packet lacks quarterly financials, Unit II capacity and funding detail, and the stock is very illiquid.

label: KRYSTAL
rationale: Size: Rs 275 crore total over five years is 21.2% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,295.96 crore, about 4% a year. Firm: work orders from VVCMC (a government body) are received for Rs 83 crore and Rs 111 crore, with the third contract implied. Routine by pattern: the company regularly wins contracts of this size (Rs 370 crore, Rs 349 crore, Rs 168 crore in 2025), so routine=true, but the TTM operating margin of 6.5% and market cap of 0.67x TTM revenue trigger the exception, and TTM revenue growth of +18.0% is above zero, so it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier: the company is rated A-/Stable and the work is a first large municipal SWM award.

label: UNIVASTU
rationale: Size: the INR 391.76 crore order (including GST, 24 months) equals 254.9% of TTM revenue of 153.70 crore on the total, or about 127% a year. Firm: a received work order from L&T. Routine: the company regularly wins large orders (244 crore in May 2025, order book 635 crore), but the cheap-valuation exception applies (market cap 80 crore is 0.52x TTM revenue, operating margin 20.4%) and TTM revenue growth is 40.6%, so it is decided as non-routine and sent to DEEP_RESEARCH. No disqualifier is shown; funding of the front-loaded working capital is the open question.

label: HECPROJECT
rationale: Size: Rs 16.35 crore stated, 11.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 142.45 crore. Firm: a received work order (binding demand), with the execution period not stated. Routine by pattern: the company has booked several orders of Rs 19 to 29 crore in the last year, so routine=true, but the market cap of about 0.98x TTM revenue triggers the cheap-valuation exception and TTM revenue growth of +70.9% is above zero, so it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier: the company is profitable with low finance cost, though the stock is illiquid and the counterparty is unnamed.

label: TANKUP
rationale: Size: Rs 8.004 crore stated, 39.4% of FY25 revenue of Rs 20.30 crore (no TTM revenue in the packet). Firm: the company has received the Indian Air Force order (binding demand). Not routine: the packet shows no earlier order disclosures, so the order is clearly bigger than anything disclosed before. No disqualifier is established, but the packet does not show whether defence bowser orders recur, and the stock had already risen sharply before the order.

label: STLTECH
rationale: Size: the stated order value is 'exceeding Rs 500 cr' for the data-centre portfolio, 11.5% of TTM revenue of Rs 4,362 cr (a floor; execution period unknown). Firm: orders secured in Q3 FY26. Not routine: no comparable sized order appears in the packet, and data-centre supply at this scale is a step-change from the telecom and interconnect wins disclosed before. No disqualifier: TTM losses are modest (PAT -Rs 43 cr) and the Rs 1,000 cr QIP of 2024 already reduced debt, though leverage (finance cost about Rs 226 cr a year) is an open research question.

label: TINNARUBR
rationale: Size: the stated total is up to Rs 75.79 cr including GST, about Rs 64.2 cr ex-GST (GST is not revenue) over two years, which is 12.7% of FY25 revenue of Rs 505 cr; the rule compares the multi-year total with annual revenue and the period is noted. Firm: a work order was received on 19 January 2026. Not routine: the packet shows no earlier order of this size and none from IOCL, so this is a new customer and product stream. No disqualifier: the company is profitable (FY25 PAT Rs 48 cr) and the packet shows no stress.

label: WAAREEENER
rationale: Size: no value is stated for the 2,000 MW order; estimated at 2,000 MW x Rs 12/Wp (assumed low-end Indian module price) = Rs 2,400 cr, or 10.9% of TTM revenue of Rs 22,060 cr. The Rs 60,000 cr order book is backlog and does not size the event. Firm: a received order from an external US developer. Not routine: about 3x the largest order in the packet (up to about 600 MW), so DEEP_RESEARCH; no disqualifier, but the estimate sits just above the 10% line and the execution period is unknown.

The company announced it secured an EPC contract, a received order, with a stated ceiling of INR 50 crore, which is 106% of TTM revenue of INR 47.08 crore (the packet notes the figure is a ceiling, not committed revenue). Prior disclosures are MoUs and one O&M contract of unstated size, so this is not business as usual, and the company is profitable with TTM operating margin of 13.2%. No disqualifier is evident; the counterparty's status is not established and the ceiling basis is the main uncertainty.

Size: a stated purchase order of USD 166,136 (about Rs 1.38 cr) is 176.9% of FY25 revenue of Rs 0.78 cr; TTM revenue cannot be computed from the two quarters shown. Firm: a received purchase order from a UAE buyer. Not routine: the packet shows no earlier export orders, so this is a first export order into a new market. No disqualifier is evident, but the order is single and the buyer's recurrence and creditworthiness are unverified, which deep research should test, so confidence is LOW.

label: ADROITINFO
rationale: Size: the stated Rs 46.0 million (about Rs 4.6 cr) five-year contract is 11.7% of TTM revenue of Rs 39.35 cr. The contract is firm (binding order), and it is routine in the sense that several similar Rs 1 cr to Rs 6 cr orders were won in 2025, but TTM operating margin is 7.8% (below 10%) and the market cap is 1.32x TTM revenue, so the thin-margin/cheap-valuation exception applies and TTM revenue growth of 38.5% is above zero, so DEEP_RESEARCH under the exception. No disqualifier, though FY25 earnings fell sharply and the share count rose 125.7%.

label: SKIPPER
rationale: Size: Rs 1,429 cr Q3 FY26 order inflow = 27.6% of TTM revenue (Rs 5,174 cr). Firm: received orders, and the book roll-forward (8,820 to 9,009 cr with Q3 revenue 1,371 cr) implies about 1,560 cr of intake, consistent with that figure. Routine: quarterly inflows of Rs 1,243 to 1,900 cr are regular, so routine=true, but the cheap-valuation exception applies (market cap 4,142 cr is 0.80x TTM revenue) with TTM revenue growth of 15.2%, so decided as not routine; TTM OPM 10.8% is not thin. No disqualifier shown; funding and dilution need checking.

Size: Rs 4.34 cr = 10.8% of FY25 revenue (Rs 40.26 cr). Firm: a received order, with execution scheduled for Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27 per the annexure. Not routine: the company's disclosed orders are machinery, and this is the first film order from a revenue stream launched in 2025. Quarterly operating margin is about 13%, so no thin-margin concern, and no disqualifier is shown; the division's economics and funding are open.

label: MARINE
rationale: Three firm orders (received, per the filing) total INR 284.39 crore excluding taxes, which is 34.1% of TTM revenue of INR 833.76 crore. The batch is about 1.6 times the largest prior disclosure (INR 174.60 crore, Nov 2025), and 2025 order inflow was only about 0.9 times revenue, so it is not routine; the TTM operating margin of 9.2% (below 10%) and TTM revenue growth of 18.0% would also satisfy the thin-margin exception if it were routine. No disqualifier is evident; the main open questions are execution margin and working capital.

label: MEGATHERM
rationale: Size: Rs 37.88 cr total order size (stated in the 29 Jan 2026 notice) = 11.8% of FY25 revenue (Rs 320.51 cr). Firm: received orders from four named private customers for supply, erection and commissioning, with advance payments. Not routine: disclosed orders so far are induction melting and bulk furnace orders, and transformers are a new product line from the facility commissioned in 2025. No disqualifier is shown, but the packet has no TTM revenue or PAT and the stock is illiquid.

label: PSPPROJECT
rationale: The 880 cr award is stated as received, equal to 32.5% of TTM revenue of 2,706 cr, so the size test passes. It is firm, and orders of this size recur for this company, so it is routine under the base test. The thin-margin and cheap-valuation exception applies (TTM OPM 6.0%, market cap 1.14x TTM revenue) and TTM revenue growth is +8.0%, so it is treated as non-routine and sent to deep research. No disqualifier: the company is not stressed (finance cost about 11 cr a quarter, credit limits available).

label: DEEDEV
rationale: Firm order inflow of 251 cr in Q3 FY26 (press release 3 Feb 2026) is 23.5% of TTM revenue of 1,066.79 cr (stated). It is routine in the sense that quarterly inflows of 320 cr and 170 cr were recent and the order book is flat, but market cap of 1,473 cr is 1.38x TTM revenue (below 1.5x), so the cheap-valuation exception applies and it is decided as non-routine; TTM revenue growth is +36%, so DEEP_RESEARCH. No disqualifier: the company is profitable (TTM PAT 81 cr) and the non-core power segment's tariff litigation does not make it stressed.

label: PRESSTONIC
rationale: Size is INR 115.09 crore stated in the LoA, about 547% of FY25 revenue of INR 21.04 crore; it spans roughly 2.5 years, so the annual run-rate is lower but still well above 10%. The LoA from an external customer is firm, and it is not business as usual because the largest prior disclosed order was about INR 9.2 crore. The page read confirmed the value and delivery window. No disqualifier shows in the packet, but losses, debt and rights-issue completion are not shown, so funding risk is open.

label: DRONE
rationale: The 17.26 cr Andhra Pradesh government work order is firm and stated at 69.3% of FY25 revenue (24.9 cr), well above the 10% threshold. It is clearly bigger than any prior disclosed order (largest previously 12 cr), so it is not routine, although the same department had awarded a mapping order in 2023. The company is loss-making (FY25 PAT -6.8 cr) with unknown debt and a recent equity raise, so funding is UNRESOLVED and confidence is LOW, but no disqualifier is evidenced in the packet.

label: JNKINDIA
rationale: The INR 1,050 crore order from JNK Global is firm (received and being executed, per the Feb 10 call) and about 156.5% of TTM revenue (INR 671 crore). Management calls it the largest order since inception, so it is not routine; even if routine, TTM operating margin of 9.6% (thin) and TTM revenue growth of 31% would allow it under the thin-margin exception. No disqualifier is evident, but the counterparty's relationship to the company and the execution period are not established in the packet. Order book check is in order_book_check.

label: GRINFRA
rationale: Management says GR has received a transmission order of about INR 3,600 crore, of which about INR 1,800 crore is GR's EPC scope: 22.0% of TTM revenue (INR 8,174 crore). It reaches GR through a group SPV, so it is treated as a firm pass-through order. It is routine by order flow, but market cap is 1.16x TTM revenue (below 1.5x) and TTM revenue growth is +7.5%, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier is evident.

label: CHANDAN
rationale: The secured Rs 26 cr government PPP contract is 11.3% of FY25 revenue of Rs 230 cr, using total value because the term is not stated. It is non-routine because it opens a public-hospital PPP channel not described in earlier disclosures. The link to the unquantified trigger is inferred and the share is close to 10% on a trailing basis, so confirming the link and term is the first deep-research step; no disqualifier is evident (profitable, funded).

A firm purchase order for Rs 14.84 cr over 12 months is about 25% of annualised 9M FY26 revenue (Rs 60 cr; FY25 revenue not in packet). No earlier order is disclosed and the customer is a first international one, so it is not routine. Confidence is low because the revenue base, the unverified counterparty and the unusually high margins are unresolved; the Rs 120.5 cr rights issue is funding context and does not size the event.

label: ANLON
rationale: The stated order of INR 28.19 crore (excluding GST) is 56.1% of FY25 revenue of 50.23 crore, the latest full year in the packet, and the company describes it as a received order (the annexure refers to an LOI, which is recorded as a contradiction). It is not routine: it is about 5.6 times the largest prior disclosed order (5.05 crore), comes from a new industrial customer, and is a manufacturing contract for ARFF vehicles. No disqualifier is evident, but the revenue base is stale (latest filing May 2025), and LOI status, delivery timing and recurrence are open for deep research.

The contract is a received purchase order, so it is firm. It is not routine: the largest previous order was about 3.5 crore, and this is a new defence ordnance revenue line. No disqualifier applies, but the awarding entity is undisclosed, capacity and funding are not shown, and the packet's 24-crore total was wrong.

label: MOREPENLAB
rationale: Stated total of about INR 825 crore is 46.2% of TTM revenue of 1,786.83 crore; it is a multi-year total, so the annual share is lower (about 15% if spread over three years), still above the 10% bar. The mandate is a binding order from an external global pharma customer, with supplies starting in 4-5 months, so it is firm. It is not routine because it opens CDMO as a new revenue stream and is described as one of the largest single CDMO mandates in company history; the company is debt-free and the market cap (about 1.34x TTM revenue) is cheap, and no disqualifier applies.

label: SIGMAADV
rationale: The 100 crore of secured defence orders is 68.6% of TTM revenue of 145.70 crore, which is a single quarter, so the true annual share may be lower; the press note says the orders are secured from MoD and defence PSUs, so they are firm. It is not routine on the packet's evidence because no earlier order disclosures exist and revenue was nil through FY25. The company is loss-making (TTM operating margin -16.1%, FY25 PAT -29.9 crore) with unknown debt, so stressed-company risk is open but not established, and the packet's zero-revenue history makes the trajectory change the question for deep research.

Two firm purchase orders from unrelated external buyers, INR 6.68 crore ex-GST in total (values confirmed in the PO annexures read with the page command), equal to 35.1% of FY25 revenue of INR 19.05 crore. There are no earlier comparable order disclosures in the packet, so the orders are not routine, and no disqualifier is evident. The company is very small and illiquid, and nine-month FY26 revenue is slowing, so deep research should confirm delivery, margin and whether the module business is recurring.

label: PATELENG
rationale: The HPPCL letter of award is firm (received after the L1 declaration) and worth INR 910.08 crore incl. GST, or about INR 771 crore ex-GST, which is 15.1% of FY25 revenue over a 30-month schedule. The company wins contracts of this size routinely (order inflow of INR 10,000-12,000 crore a year, roughly twice revenue), so it is routine, but the P/S of 0.51 is below the 1.5x cheap-valuation threshold and TTM revenue growth is +4.4%, so the exception applies and it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier found (the state-owned counterparty is external, and debt and promoter pledge are context, not a stressed balance sheet); the Dorjilung pre-construction award (INR 230.70 crore, about 4.5% of revenue) adds little on its own.

label: READYMIX
rationale: Firm PO for Rs 15.80 crore excluding GST, executed in about 22 weeks, equal to 21.6% of FY25 revenue of Rs 73.28 crore (TTM revenue is not in the packet). Not routine on the packet: no earlier order disclosures show a normal flow, and this single order is well above anything the company has disclosed. Market cap of about Rs 96 crore is about 1.3x FY25 revenue, so the cheap-valuation test would also be met if the order were routine. No disqualifier and no sign of stress; the main gaps are margin, funding and order history.

label: HILTON
rationale: Stated consideration of about Rs 720 crore over 24 months (about Rs 360 crore a year, roughly 160% of annual revenue) against TTM revenue of Rs 224.5 crore (320.7% on the total basis). The contract is received and firm, though sample and prototype approvals gate payment. Not routine: a first defence ordnance contract, far above any order in the packet. The thin TTM operating margin (4.9%) and low valuation (P/S 0.21) would also satisfy the routine-exception test, since TTM revenue grew 47.8%. No disqualifier found; the company was profitable on a TTM basis.

Firm received order of Rs 12.57 crore including GST (Rs 10.65 crore ex-GST), with delivery due by 14 April 2026. That is 1,868% of FY25 revenue of Rs 0.57 crore and still over 200% against the known trailing quarters (about Rs 4.5 crore). Not routine: the packet shows no earlier order disclosures and this is a commodity supply line new to the company. No disqualifier is met on the packet (losses are large but no high debt is shown, so the stressed test is not met); funding and delivery feasibility are open, so confidence is LOW.

label: SRM
rationale: Size: the 4 Apr 2026 MSIDC contract of INR 483 cr is 59.8% of TTM revenue of INR 807 cr; the execution period is not stated. Firm: contract awarded to the company. Not routine: it is about 3x the largest prior award in the packet (INR 155 cr, Oct 2025) and about 1.5x the 9M FY26 order inflow; the cheap-valuation exception (P/S 1.35x, TTM growth +98%) would also give DEEP_RESEARCH. No disqualifier; the company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 81 cr).

label: JKIL
rationale: Size: the company's contract price of INR 1,184 cr over 24 months is 20.5% of TTM revenue of INR 5,770 cr (the JV total is INR 2,360 cr). Firm: LoA received by the JV. Routine: the company wins INR 1,000 cr-plus orders several times a year, so the order is routine, but the market cap is 0.62x TTM revenue and TTM operating margin is 14.2%, so the cheap-valuation exception applies with TTM revenue growth of +5.2%. Decided as non-routine, it is DEEP_RESEARCH; no disqualifier applies.

label: CHAMUNDA
rationale: Size: the filing states INR 63.47 crore incl. GST, INR 53.79 crore ex-GST, over 36 months; against FY25 revenue of INR 25.29 crore that is 212.7% in total, about 71% a year. Firm: a letter of award received from a government company on 1 April 2026. Not routine: it is the largest order disclosed by the company and opens a multi-year O&M service stream, versus the earlier INR 30 crore GETCO order. No disqualifier is evident (counterparty is unrelated; no promoter interest), but the packet's financials stop at June 2025 so margin and funding must be researched.

label: THERMAX
rationale: Size: the INR 1,600 cr boiler package order is 15.5% of TTM revenue of INR 10,344 cr, over an execution period not stated. Firm: order secured by the wholly owned subsidiary from an external power projects company. Not routine: it is about 2.8x the largest order in the packet (INR 580 cr, Nov 2025) and sits in the 800 MW utility-boiler segment. The thin-margin exception would also give DEEP_RESEARCH, since TTM revenue growth is +2.7%. No disqualifier; PAT is INR 681 cr TTM.

label: DUGLOBAL
rationale: The filing states the company 'has been awarded' a three-year CPV contract for the Embassy of India, Kuwait, worth about Rs 90 crore; against FY2024-25 revenue of Rs 48.2 crore that is 186.9% on the three-year total (about 62% a year). The contract is firm on its award wording despite the L1 headline, and it is not routine: it is roughly 15-18 times the company's earlier overseas visa contracts and opens a GCC market. No disqualifier: the counterparty is a government mission, the contract is recurring rather than one-off, and profits are positive, though the packet's financials are stale and funding is unresolved.

label: DSSL
rationale: The Rs 750.82 cr RBI award is 55.6% of TTM revenue of Rs 1,350.74 cr (stated) and is a received, firm order. Dynacons wins private-cloud contracts regularly, but at about three times its largest prior single award this is clearly bigger than anything disclosed, so it is not routine; the cheap-valuation exception (price to sales 1.23, TTM OPM 10.3%, TTM revenue growth +10.7%) would also allow deep research. No disqualifier applies: it is a single named award, the company is profitable and growing, and the packet shows no distress.

label: NITCO
rationale: The 66.65 Cr order is 12.3% of TTM revenue (542 Cr) and is firm, since purchase orders were received per the 12 May 2026 filing. Prestige has placed repeated orders (105 Cr in Dec 2024, 19 Cr in Sep 2025, and about 347 Cr cumulative), so the order is routine on its own. The thin-margin exception applies (TTM operating margin 3.9%, market cap about 4.3x TTM revenue), and TTM revenue growth is 72%, so it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier found, since the restructuring is in the past and FY26 funding was raised through preferential issues.

label: SEPC
rationale: The 521.46 Cr letter of award is firm and equals 58% of TTM revenue of 898.47 Cr, but the company's order inflow is routine (5,954 Cr in nine months, about 6.6 times TTM revenue). The thin-margin exception applies (TTM operating margin 9.1%) and TTM revenue growth is 43%, so it is decided as non-routine and sent to deep research. The main uncertainties are SEPC's share of the JV, which the packet does not give, and the company's restructuring history (promoter pledges of 71%), so confidence is low.

label: TEXRAIL
rationale: The Letter of Award for 4,045 Cr is 92% of TTM revenue (4,377 Cr) and is firm, since an LoA from an unrelated external buyer was received. It is clearly bigger than anything the company has disclosed (the largest prior award was 219 Cr) and is its first large export order, so it is not routine. No disqualifier is evident; the open questions are the execution period, the conversion of the LoA into a contract, and funding, and the audit opinion on FY26 results is modified.

label: QUICKHEAL
